title: Best Gaming Benchmark PCs for Everyday Play: What to Look For
summary: Learn how to choose a balanced gaming benchmark PC for smooth 1080p and 1440p play, multitasking, and long-term value.
body_text: If you’re shopping for a gaming desktop that can do more than post a flashy benchmark number, you’re in the right place. The best everyday gaming PC is the one that feels fast, stays stable, and gives you the performance you actually notice while you play. That usually means a well-matched CPU and GPU, plus enough memory and storage to keep everything moving without slowdowns. For most gamers, the sweet spot lives between entry-level and high-end. You want enough power for smooth 1080p and 1440p gaming, with extra room for voice chat, streaming, browser tabs, and whatever else you run in the background. That kind of balance is what makes a benchmark PC feel like a smart buy instead of a spec sheet flex. Overview: What Defines a Good Everyday Gaming Benchmark PC? A strong everyday gaming benchmark PC should deliver consistency first. Peak frame rates are nice, but the real win is smooth frame pacing, responsive load times, and the kind of performance that holds up in actual games. A modern 6-core or 8-core CPU, 16 GB to 32 GB of RAM, and an SSD can make a huge difference in day-to-day feel compared with older systems that only look similar on paper. If you’re trying to decide whether a desktop is worth it, ask a simple question: does it fit the way you play? The best choice is usually a PC that can handle competitive titles, open-world games, and everyday multitasking without constant tweaking. If you want something that works well after work, for shared household use, or as an all-around desktop, real-world benchmark performance matters more than chasing the highest score. Key Features to Prioritize When you’re comparing gaming desktops, focus on the parts that have the biggest impact on your experience: CPU: A modern 6-core or 8-core processor helps with game logic, background tasks, and smoother multitasking. GPU: The graphics card matters most for gaming performance, especially at 1440p and with higher settings. Memory: 16 GB is the practical minimum; 32 GB is a better long-term choice for heavy multitasking. Storage: A fast NVMe SSD improves boot times, game launches, and patch installs. Cooling and power delivery: Stable thermals help maintain performance during long gaming sessions. A balanced build almost always beats an uneven one. A powerful GPU paired with a weak CPU can still stutter in CPU-heavy games, while an overbuilt CPU with a modest graphics card may not give you the gaming results you were hoping for. Matching the parts properly is what makes a benchmark PC feel impressive in daily use, not just in charts. Hands-on Performance: What You Should Expect For everyday gaming, the best benchmark PC should feel smooth in real titles, not just look good in synthetic tests. Competitive shooters benefit from high, stable frame rates, while larger AAA games need enough GPU muscle and CPU headroom to keep things steady. A well-built desktop should also handle Discord, game launchers, and a few browser tabs without turning your session into a lagfest. In practical terms, the right benchmark PC for most shoppers is one that can handle 1080p gaming comfortably and still hold up at 1440p with sensible settings. If your game library mixes esports and big story-driven releases, that flexibility is more useful than a single headline result. Simple Comparison Table The breakdown below shows the kind of balance most everyday gamers should aim for. Entry-level: Best for 1080p esports and lighter games, but may require lowered settings in new AAA titles. Midrange benchmark PC: Best balance for 1080p high refresh or 1440p gaming with better longevity. High-end: Great for maximum settings and demanding workloads, but often unnecessary for everyday gaming. Pros and Cons of a Balanced Gaming Benchmark PC Pros Better real-world gaming consistency than spec-heavy but unbalanced systems. Handles modern games, multitasking, and daily use with less compromise. Usually offers stronger value than top-tier builds for most players. More likely to stay relevant for several years without immediate upgrades. Cons May not deliver the absolute highest FPS in benchmark charts. Can be less exciting on paper than premium flagship desktops. Some prebuilt models may prioritize appearance over cooling or component quality. Final Verdict: Who Is This PC Best For? The best benchmark PC for everyday gaming is a smart pick for players who want a dependable, balanced desktop that performs well in real games without overspending. It’s ideal if you care more about smooth gameplay, quick loading, and long-term value than chasing the biggest benchmark score. If your routine includes esports, AAA titles, streaming, or a mix of work and play, this is the category worth targeting. For most shoppers, the formula is simple: choose a modern midrange CPU, a capable GPU, at least 16 GB of RAM, and an NVMe SSD. That combination delivers the most practical gaming experience and the least buyer’s remorse over time. Ready to buy? Focus first on the GPU, CPU, RAM, and SSD, because those parts have the biggest effect on real gaming smoothness and load times. For most players, a modern 6-core or 8-core CPU, a capable midrange GPU, 16 GB to 32 GB of RAM, and an NVMe SSD is the most practical combination. Is a midrange gaming PC better value than a high-end build? Yes, in many cases a midrange gaming PC is the smarter buy because it delivers strong 1080p and 1440p performance without pushing you into premium pricing. High-end systems can be impressive, but the extra performance is often harder to notice in everyday play unless you game at very high settings or use demanding workloads. Can a balanced benchmark PC handle both AAA and esports games? Absolutely, as long as the CPU and GPU are matched well. Esports titles benefit from stable high frame rates, while AAA games need enough graphics power and memory to maintain smooth settings and consistent frame pacing. How much RAM should a gaming desktop have in 2026? 16 GB is still the practical minimum for most gamers, especially if you usually play one game at a time. If you stream, keep many apps open, or want more future-proofing, 32 GB gives you more headroom and can make the system feel more responsive. What should I verify before buying a prebuilt gaming benchmark PC? Check the exact CPU and GPU models, plus the cooling, power supply quality, and SSD capacity. You should also confirm the warranty, return policy, and current stock status so you know what support and availability to expect after purchase. title: I Inherited a $400k IRA. The 10-Year Rule Could Hand the IRS a Third of It Unless I Act Now
summary: Waiting to empty an inherited IRA could leave you with a bigger tax bill. Here's how timing your withdrawals can affect taxes.
body_text: The IRS generally gives you 10 years to empty an inherited IRA, but that flexibility can work against you. Waiting until the deadline to withdraw may mean taking the entire balance in a shorter window, and larger withdrawals could push you into a higher tax bracket. Taking smaller amounts over the full decade could help you keep more of your inheritance out of the IRS’s hands. One Tax Mistake You Could Face With the 10-Year Rule If you inherit a traditional IRA from someone other than your spouse, you generally must empty the account by December 31 of the 10th year after the original owner’s death. The SECURE Act replaced the lifetime “ stretch IRA ” for most non-spouse beneficiaries with this 10-year deadline . The IRS generally doesn’t tell you how much to withdraw each year. It only requires that the account be empty by the deadline. If the original owner had already started taking required minimum distributions (RMDs) , you would likely need to continue taking annual RMDs during the 10-year period while still emptying the account by the last year. That flexibility is where beneficiaries could make a costly mistake. The 10-year rule sets a deadline, but it leaves you to decide when and how much to withdraw after taking any RMDs. Those decisions affect how much of your inheritance you could keep after taxes. The Math Behind the Potential Tax Hit To show how withdrawals can affect your taxes, let’s assume that you inherit a $400,000 traditional IRA and earn $90,000 annually as a single filer. Using the 2026 federal income tax brackets , the table below breaks down your total federal tax if you withdraw the full $400,000 in the 10th year, which would bring your taxable income to $490,000. Bracket Income Taxed at This Rate Tax Owed 10% $12,400 $1,240 ($12,400 × 10%) 12% $38,000 ($50,400 − $12,400) $4,560 ($38,000 × 12%) 22% $55,300 ($105,700 − $50,400) $12,166 ($55,300 × 22%) 24% $96,075 ($201,775 − $105,700) $23,058 ($96,075 × 24%) 32% $54,450 ($256,225 − $201,775) $17,424 ($54,450 × 32%) 35% $233,775 ($490,000 − $256,225) $81,821 ($233,775 × 35%) Total $490,000 $140,269 Your $90,000 salary alone would owe $14,512 in tax, and that’s already part of the $140,269 total above. So the IRA withdrawal itself adds up to $125,757 of that bill. For a comparison, let’s assume that you divide your inheritance into $40,000 withdrawals each year. This would make your taxable income in the first year $130,000. Your salary and IRA withdrawal would fill the bottom four brackets. Bracket Income Taxed at This Rate Tax Owed Per Year 10% $12,400 $1,240 ($12,400 × 10%) 12% $38,000 ($50,400 − $12,400) $4,560 ($38,000 × 12%) 22% $55,300 ($105,700 − $50,400) $12,166 ($55,300 × 22%) 24% $24,300 ($130,000 − $105,700) $5,832 ($24,300 × 24%) Total Per Year $130,000 $23,798 In this example, your $90,000 salary alone would still owe $14,512, so the $40,000 withdrawal accounts for $9,286 of that bill. Multiplied across the full 10-year period, you would owe $92,860 in total federal tax on the inheritance , saving roughly $32,900 when compared with a full lump sum withdrawal in year 10. Withdrawal Strategy Federal Tax Attributable to the IRA Withdrawal Full $400,000 in year 10 $125,757 $40,000 per year for 10 years $92,860 Difference $32,897 Keep in mind that if your salary or other income changes in a given year, the tax owed on each withdrawal would change too. A financial advisor could help you model how a lump-sum compares with a spread-out withdrawal strategy for your specific situation. Why Having a Plan in Year One Matters Beneficiaries often postpone planning because the deadline is years away. Starting with a withdrawal plan in the first year can give you more time to adjust distributions as your income changes instead of making last-minute decisions when the deadline approaches. Putting a withdrawal plan in place during the first year gives you a framework to revisit over time instead of making decisions under pressure as the deadline approaches. A financial advisor can help you build a long-term withdrawal schedule and adjust it as your financial situation changes. Photo credit: ©iStock.com/skynesher, ©iStock.com/seb_ra

title: Cómo detectar productos que no se venden en tu tienda | Treinta
summary: Detecta productos que no se venden en tu tienda con 3 indicadores y una rutina de minutos. Reduce pérdidas, libera capital y aplica acciones inmediatas hoy.
body_text: En casi cualquier tienda pequeña hay productos que llevan semanas, o meses, ocupando espacio sin venderse. No son visibles a primera vista porque están mezclados con el inventario que sí mueve, pero su costo ya está pagado y el dinero está atrapado ahí hasta que alguien lo detecte y tome una decisión. Ese inventario muerto es una de las fugas de capital más silenciosas de un negocio pequeño. En esta guía encontrarás cómo identificarlo con datos concretos, qué hacer para recuperar ese dinero y cómo evitar que vuelva a acumularse. Las señales de que tienes inventario que no rota El inventario muerto no aparece en la caja ni en el estado de resultados. Se detecta comparando lo que compraste contra lo que vendiste en un periodo dado. El indicador más directo es la antigüedad del stock. Cualquier producto que lleve más de 30 días sin venderse en una tienda de alta rotación (abarrotes, farmacia) es una señal de alerta. En tiendas de menor rotación (ferretería, papelería), el umbral se mueve a 60 o 90 días. Cuando un producto no se vende en dos o tres veces su ciclo normal de compra, ya es inventario problemático. El segundo indicador es la diferencia entre lo que compraste y lo que vendiste. Si compraste 24 latas de atún en enero y en febrero solo habías vendido 8, tienes 16 unidades paradas. Si eso se repite el siguiente mes sin ninguna acción, el problema crece. El tercero es el valor del inventario en relación a las ventas. Si el valor total de tu inventario representa más de 45 días de ventas, hay productos que no están rotando a la velocidad correcta. Para entender mejor cómo funciona la rotación de inventario y cómo mejorarla, el blog de Treinta sobre qué es la rotación de inventario y cómo mejorarla tiene el cálculo completo. En Treinta puedes ver el historial de movimientos por producto y detectar cuáles llevan más tiempo sin salir, sin necesidad de revisar físicamente cada anaquel. ¿Ya usas Treinta? Descarga la app y empieza a detectar tu inventario muerto hoy. Cómo clasificar tu catálogo para encontrar los problemas La clasificación ABC convierte una lista de cientos de productos en tres grupos manejables que tienen estrategias distintas. Los productos clase A son los que generan entre el 60% y el 70% de las ventas. En una tienda de abarrotes suelen ser entre 20 y 30 productos: refrescos, leche, huevo, galletas, papel higiénico. Estos necesitan control estrecho porque un quiebre de stock en cualquiera de ellos afecta directamente los ingresos. Los productos clase B representan entre el 20% y el 25% de las ventas. Se venden con regularidad pero sin la frecuencia de los A. Requieren revisión semanal y pedidos programados pero sin la urgencia de los primeros. Los productos clase C son los que generan el 5% o menos de las ventas y representan entre el 50% y el 70% del catálogo. Aquí es donde vive el inventario muerto. Dentro del grupo C, hay productos que se venden ocasionalmente y tienen sentido mantener, y hay productos que simplemente no se venden y están ahí por inercia o porque "algún día alguien los va a pedir". Para hacer esa clasificación necesitas el historial de ventas por producto de los últimos 60 o 90 días. Con ese dato puedes ordenar el catálogo de mayor a menor número de ventas y los del fondo de la lista son los candidatos a revisar primero. El software de control de inventarios de Treinta registra cada venta por producto y permite ver ese historial de movimientos sin necesidad de llevar un cuaderno separado por cada artículo. Qué hacer con el inventario que no se vende Detectar el inventario muerto es el primer paso. El segundo es decidir qué hacer con él, y esa decisión tiene urgencia porque el tiempo juega en contra. La primera opción es la promoción dirigida. Hacer visible un producto que nadie pide porque nadie lo nota suele ser suficiente para moverlo. Una posición diferente en el estante, una etiqueta que diga "pruébalo" o una sugerencia directa al cliente cuando está pagando pueden generar ventas de productos que llevan semanas quietos sin mayor esfuerzo. La segunda opción es el bundle. Incluir el producto lento dentro de un paquete con uno de alta rotación crea un incentivo sin que el cliente sienta que le están vendiendo un artículo difícil de colocar. La tortilla que no se vende sola puede salir bien acompañada de la salsa que sí tiene demanda en un combo de 35 pesos. La tercera opción es el descuento de liquidación. Si el producto tiene fecha de caducidad próxima o si definitivamente no tiene demanda en ese negocio, mejor recuperar parte del costo ahora que tirar el producto más adelante. Un descuento del 20% al 30% que mueve el producto esta semana es mejor que un 100% de pérdida en un mes. La cuarta opción, la más difícil de aceptar, es dejar de resurtir. Si un producto no se vende ni con promoción ni en bundle ni con descuento, ese espacio y ese capital están mejor invertidos en algo que sí genera rotación. Decidir no resurtir un producto que no funciona no es una pérdida: es liberar capital que estaba atrapado en el anaquel. Para evitar que el inventario muerto se acumule en el futuro, el blog de Treinta sobre cómo evitar el quiebre de stock y sobre cómo calcular el punto de reorden tienen las herramientas para comprar lo correcto en el momento correcto. Cómo prevenir que vuelva a acumularse El inventario muerto casi siempre viene de dos fuentes: comprar por costumbre sin revisar la rotación, o comprar porque "estaba en promoción" sin verificar si realmente se vende. La práctica que más previene la acumulación es revisar la rotación antes de hacer cada pedido. Si el último pedido de un producto todavía tiene más del 50% en el estante, esa es una señal de que la cantidad o la frecuencia de compra necesita ajustarse. La segunda práctica es tener un periodo de prueba para productos nuevos. Antes de comprar dos cajas de un artículo que nunca has vendido, compra cuatro o cinco unidades para medir si tiene demanda. Si en tres semanas no se vendieron, ya tienes la respuesta sin haber comprometido capital importante. Los reportes y estadísticas de Treinta facilitan esa revisión previa al pedido mostrando el historial de ventas por producto de los últimos 30 días. Con ese dato, la decisión de cuánto pedir deja de ser una estimación y se convierte en un número respaldado por lo que realmente ocurrió en el negocio. Conoce todas las funcionalidades en treinta.co/mx . Detectar el inventario muerto esta semana y tomar acción sobre él puede liberar capital que llevas meses pagando sin retorno. Descarga Treinta y revisa el historial de movimientos de tus productos. ¿Tienes preguntas sobre cómo manejar el inventario de tu tienda? Contáctanos. Preguntas frecuentes sobre cómo detectar productos que no se están vendiendo en mi tienda ¿Cuánto tiempo es razonable para que un producto esté sin venderse antes de tomar acción? En tiendas de alta rotación como abarrotes, 30 días sin venta ya es señal de alerta. En negocios de menor rotación como ferreterías, el umbral es de 60 a 90 días. Lo importante es definir ese límite por adelantado y revisarlo con disciplina. ¿Qué hago si el producto que no se vende ya lo pagué y no puedo devolverlo? Evalúa si es mejor venderlo con descuento ahora o esperar. Si tiene fecha de caducidad próxima, la decisión es urgente. Si es un producto sin caducidad, puedes intentar primero con cambio de exhibición o bundle antes de bajar el precio. ¿Cómo sé si el problema es el producto o la forma en que lo exhibo? Cambia su ubicación en el estante a un lugar de mayor visibilidad durante dos semanas. Si empieza a venderse, el problema era la exhibición. Si sigue sin moverse, el producto no tiene demanda en tu negocio específico. ¿Puedo devolver al proveedor productos que no se vendieron? Depende de los acuerdos que tengas. Algunos proveedores permiten devoluciones dentro de cierto plazo, especialmente en productos perecederos. Negocia esa condición al momento de la compra si es posible. ¿Cuánto capital es normal tener atrapado en inventario? El inventario no debería representar más de 30 a 45 días de costo de ventas. Si supera ese rango, hay productos que no rotan al ritmo que necesitan para ser eficientes con el capital del negocio.

title: Sensor Technology Is Invading Every Facet of Our Lives… And It’s Spectacular!
summary: What kind of sensors are in the objects we use everyday? Learn how much technology is really crammed into everyday devices.
body_text: Common devices are being equipped with more and more sensing technology to give users greater control over their everyday lives. It’s easy to fall into the trap of thinking about sensors in a purely abstract way. Sure, we know current and emerging sensor technology is crucial to the expansion of the IoT, which is forecast to revolutionize everything from agriculture to city management. We’re also intimately familiar with a sensor fusion device (one capable of integrating the outputs from multiple different sensors) that is likely only a few feet away from us at any given time—our smartphones. These now-essential machines are equipped with GPS sensors, accelerometers, capacitive touchscreens, light sensors, and IR scanners, among many others. But as technological proliferation grows by leaps and bounds and we move towards the trillion sensor universe, even the most mundane devices and appliance in our daily lives are becoming awash in sensing technology. These deceptively smart devices may resemble their forbears at a glance, but thanks to their ability to understand the world around them through sensing technology, their capabilities far outstrip those of their predecessors. Here are just a few examples of devices that we’ve used for decades, and how recent additions of modern sensor technology have taken their functionality to the next level. Take, for instance, the humble coffee maker. For many folks, it’s an essential part of their morning (perhaps the essential part). And while luddites may still cling to their French presses, modern coffee machines are often loaded with sensing technology. The latest models include everything from touchscreen interfaces, AI-based voice control integration, and the ability to precisely control nearly any variable you can imagine during the brewing process. All of these inputs and systems rely on various forms of sensing technology to translate conditions in the outside world into data that the device can understand and react to. To make this process seamless, high-tech coffee machines utilize touchscreens as their main human machine interface (HMI), with the number of physical buttons and switches on the units being kept to a minimum. Optical sensors and force sensors detect the presence and size of cups in which to dispense the machine’s contents. Meanwhile, water temperature sensors and pressure sensors are all monitored precisely, ensuring each cup is made to specification every time. Another group of sensors even proactively prevents problems by using force detectors to make sure all components securely in place before operation. Modern video game controllers go far beyond simple joysticks and electronic button inputs. These advanced HMI devices are not only far more complex than their predecessors, to keep frustrated gamers from throwing them at the wall, they must also be precise and responsive. The latest generations of controllers from the big three console makers (Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo) have included gadgetry like IR sensors, built-in voice commands, haptic feedback, variable pressure sensors, capacitive touchscreens for fingertip controls, and gyroscopic sensors and accelerometers to detect motion. The push into virtual reality introduces even more advanced interfaces that help gamers more fully immerse themselves in the experience. A bevy of motion detectors in the headset and hand controllers are paired with external optical or IR sensors that track the user’s motion in 3D space. The most recent VR hardware releases from Oculus take the technology even further by dispensing with the external sensors, instead relying on cameras embedded in the headset and predictive algorithms to track motion without needing to set up a room specifically for VR. Of course, while gaming is one of the largest applications for VR, the same technology is being used in more practical applications. These advanced bundles of sensors can also help professionals approach their business in novel ways. For example, car manufacturers use VR to visualize their concepts in full-size 3D space without needing to build models or prototypes. In the age of COVID-19, these wonderful sensor fusion devices can allow people quarantined in their homes to attend virtual events like concerts and stand-up comedy shows. This category is a bit more iterative than those we delved into previously. It comes as no surprise that automobiles have long employed a wide range of mechanical and, more recently, electronic sensors to keep track of almost everything going on under the hood. This monitoring is so comprehensive that nowadays mechanics can often just rely on error reports generated by this array of sensors to diagnose any given problem. An exhaustive list of all the sensing technologies integrated into engine management systems would be interminable, but examples include everything from airflow and voltage sensors to speed and temperature measurement devices. Meanwhile, inside the cabin, sensing technology has been utilized to enhance functionality as well as occupant safety and comfort. Capacitive touchscreens are often employed as the HMI device of choice when interacting with navigation/infotainment systems. Meanwhile, pressure sensors in passenger seats can detect the weight of a child and turn off the airbag, protecting them from serious injury. However, when it comes to truly revolutionary uses for sensors by automobile designers, the most exciting developments are in the augmented and automated driving sector. These technologies can range from relatively simple lane departure systems that correct a vehicle’s trajectory if the car begins to veer out of its lane, to parking assistance for the dreaded tight parallel spot, to systems that are advanced enough to take over nearly all driving duties. However, such being tasked with such important duties call for a system with built-in redundancy to minimize the chance for mishaps. In these autonomous and semi-autonomous driving scenarios, cars employ optical sensors, sonar, IR scanners, and Lidar, among others. Lidar is an especially fascinating technology, as it uses laser light to map the surrounding environment with incredible fidelity. By combining all of these various sensors, we can create self-driving cars that not only safely follow traffic laws, but also have the ability to react to unexpected events more quickly than a human driver ever could. As our first example showed, kitchen appliances are ripe for sensor integration and sensor fusion. In fact, some of the biggest names in electronics, such as Samsung and LG, have introduced ranges of smart appliances awash in sensors. And just as the television is the center of a home entertainment system, the heart of most smart kitchen setups is the refrigerator. Not only does it serve as a hub, it is also the device that combines the most interesting array of sensing technologies. Localized temperature sensors allow the owner to set different cooling levels for different zones of the refrigerator. Even more magically, optical sensors inside the unit are used to monitor its contents, tracking the food inventory and adding replacement items to a list when they are depleted. Of course, it wouldn’t be much of a smart device without a fancy capacitive touchscreen display, which not only controls fridge functions, but also facilitates extra features like sticking virtual notes to the door, pulling up recipes from the Internet, displaying a live video feed from inside the cabinet, and even communicating with other connected devices—each of which relies on its own set of sensing technologies to carry out its tasks. While these features may seem flashy, sensors on refrigerators are also being used in much more practical ways. Some models are equipped with force sensors or gesture sensors that can open the door with a gentle touch or wave of your foot, respectively. Anyone who has struggled to open the fridge with arms full of groceries will understand how this simple sensor application can be a godsend. Wearable technology that constantly monitors and records your physiological state as well as data from your external environment is about as intimate as sensor technology gets. But this new product category has benefited from being introduced in devices with which people are already comfortable. Currently, the most prevalent wearable sensing devices are smart watches (or sports bands) and ear-worn accessories (most often incorporated into earbuds). Two of the most common features these devices incorporate are footstep counters (pedometers)—which utilize data collected from accelerometers—and heart rate monitors, which typically comprise a green led light and a sensor that detects variations in the light reflected back from the wearer’s skin. But these devices have gradually incorporated more and more features, such as blood oxygen level sensors, sleep cycle monitor, ambient decibel sensors, electrocardiograms (ECGs), and altimeters. In fact, smart watch market leader Apple’s newest iWatch commercials focus entirely on health monitoring sensors built into the device, completely ignoring core features that duplicate smartphone functionality like receiving emails and text messages—an early selling point for smart watches. Beyond these current-generation applications, wearable sensors offer the promise of bringing meaningful changes to people’s lives. For instance, blood sugar monitors embedded into fabrics could give people suffering with diabetes immediate warning if their blood sugar enters dangerous territory. The flexibility of printed electronics make them an obvious candidate around which to build these sensors. Though the growth of the wearables market has faced an unexpected hit resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic—it is expected to grow 8 percent this year versus 89 percent last year—the segment is forecast to expand at a CAGR of 9.4 percent over the next four years. However, given the innovative applications and prototypes for new wearables in the works, the technology has the potential to become pervasive. COVID-19 may even turn out to be a blessing in disguise for the segment. Fitbit has announced it is working on algorithms that would employ sensor fusion to determine if a person might be infected with the disease by monitoring their resting heart rate, breathing rate, and heart rate variability. This timely application could not have been predicted when the Fitbit was first designed, but by analyzing the sensor fusion data it is already collecting in a new way, it is able to adapt to solve a new problem. It’s a wonderful illustration of how versatile the uses for sensor data truly are. We hope this has given you a better idea of the depth and breadth of sensor applications. Even the most mundane devices can benefit from the integration of sensor technology, and it can be done in such a seamless way that users won’t even be aware of all of the technological wizardry taking place. Have we sparked your imagination? Get in touch with our knowledgeable team of engineers to learn how sensor integration can enhance your products.

title: LivSmart Studios by Hilton Pensacola I-10 North Davis Highway Opens in Pensacola, Florida

Designed for stays of 10 nights or longer, LivSmart Studios by Hilton provides a comfortable, functional long-stay experience backed by the value, consistency and hospitality guests expect from Hilton. PENSACOLA, Fla. – LivSmart Studios by Hilton Pensacola I-10 North Davis Highway is now open, bringing Hilton’s newest long-stay brand to Florida’s Gulf Coast. Located at 7077 Plantation Road, the hotel is owned by 3H Group and managed by LBA Hospitality. Designed for guests staying 10 nights or longer, LivSmart Studios by Hilton delivers a thoughtfully designed long-stay experience that combines comfort and functionality with the consistency, value and hospitality travelers expect when they stay with Hilton. As the fourth LivSmart Studios property to open, this hotel reflects the brand’s continued momentum and growing presence across the country, with many more locations slated to open this year and beyond. LivSmart Studios by Hilton - Lobby Rendering The Pensacola hotel is the second LivSmart Studios property opened by 3H Group and managed by LBA Hospitality, following the opening of LivSmart Studios Tullahoma in 2025 as the brand’s very first hotel. LivSmart Studios by Hilton Pensacola I-10 North Davis Highway features the brand’s signature apartment-style studios with fully equipped kitchens, including full-size refrigerators, stovetops and microwaves. title: We Have $1.6 Million in IRAs. When One of Us Dies, the Survivor’s Tax Rate Nearly Doubles
summary: Losing a spouse can also mean losing your lower tax bracket. It has a name: the widow's penalty. Here's how you could be affected.
body_text: If you and your spouse have $1.6 million saved across your IRAs, and one of you dies, the surviving spouse could pay a much higher tax rate on the same retirement income. The best opportunity to reduce that future tax bill is often while you’re both alive. But if you’re already the surviving spouse, there may still be ways to soften the tax hit. The Widow’s Penalty They call this tax hike the “widow’s penalty” because it hits surviving spouses. The hike is triggered by a change in filing status, which usually switches from married filing jointly to single for the year after the spouse dies, unless the survivor qualifies for another filing status. Higher tax brackets then kick in at much lower income levels. For 2026, married couples filing jointly stay in the 12% bracket until $100,800 of taxable income. Single filers leave that 12% bracket at just $50,400 and land in the 22% bracket well before hitting six figures. 1 A couple with $100,000 in taxable income is still sitting in the 12% bracket. That same $100,000, filed single, reaches the 22% bracket instead. The marginal rate on the top portion is nearly double, even though not a dollar of income actually changed. A financial advisor can help you calculate how much the widow’s penalty could add to your future taxes. What That Could Look Like on a $1.6 Million IRA Assuming the surviving spouse is 75 and owns a $1.6 million IRA, the required minimum distribution (RMD) would be about $65,041. This estimate is based on the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table factor of 24.6 ($1,600,000 ÷ 24.6 = $65,041). 2 Here’s how that $65,041 would get taxed under each filing status, assuming the full amount represents taxable income and no tax credits apply: Bracket Joint Return Single Return 10% $2,480 (on first $24,800) $1,240 (on first $12,400) 12% $4,829 (on remaining $40,241) $4,560 (on next $38,000) 22% — $3,221 (on remaining $14,641) Total Federal Tax $7,309 $9,021 Only the top portion of the distribution moves from the 12% bracket to the 22% bracket. Most of the distribution is still taxed at the lower rates, which is why the total federal tax bill goes up from $7,309 to $9,021, an increase of roughly 23% ($9,021 − $7,309 = $1,712). Strategies to Reduce the Tax Hit If both spouses are still alive, a Roth conversion done now can lock in today’s lower joint rate before the higher single rate ever applies. Here’s a simple example using a $100,000 Roth conversion, assuming the additional $100,000 falls entirely within the applicable tax bracket in each case: Example Bracket Taxable Amount Federal Tax Roth conversion now while filing jointly 12% $100,000 $12,000 Withdrawal later while filing single 22% $100,000 $22,000 Difference $10,000 Your actual numbers will vary depending on how much of the conversion or withdrawal lands in each bracket. If you’re already the surviving spouse, a Roth conversion can still make sense in some cases, though the narrower single brackets can make it a more expensive move than it would have been while filing jointly. A financial advisor can help you decide whether a Roth conversion or another strategy makes sense for your taxes. Photo credit: ©iStock.com/Jelena Stanojkovic, ©iStock.com/RealPeopleGroup. title: FaceTime, Zoom and Ring Cameras Are Warping Our Reality
summary: Staring at ourselves on screens, on video and on social media is taking us to a dark place.
body_text: Staring at ourselves on screens, on video and on social media is taking us to a dark place.
